title: Decompose entity JSONB blobs into normalized tables and perform online migration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several control-plane tables store large JSONB payloads (audit_metadata, entity_blobs) that have grown over time. The wide rows and redundant nested fields cause query amplification, slow index scans, and high WAL churn for updates. This ticket proposes extracting frequently queried attributes into normalized columns/tables and introducing a safe, online migration path with dual-write and view compatibility layers.
background: We observed 95th percentile read latencies on tenant-scoped queries increase by ~2x when JSONB blobs are scanned during joins. Current mitigations (materialized views and GC rules) are brittle and complicate rollbacks. Normalizing will reduce row width, enable targeted partial indexes, and improve planner estimates.
goals: Identify 3-5 high-value JSONB attributes to extract that unlock indexability
Design normalized tables and FK relationships with minimal additional joins
Implement an online migrator that backfills data without blocking writes
Maintain API compatibility via read views or compatibility layer until deprecation
Reduce average row width for hot control-plane tables by >= 30% and lower 95th percentile query latency by >= 20% for targeted routes
acceptance_criteria: Backfill job completes for a full production tenant set in staging and runs within expected window (<= 6 hours for pilot tenants)
No visible elevation in error rate or tail latency in canary during dual-write period
Partial indexes on extracted columns show measurable planner improvement in explain plans
Compatibility view returns identical shape for existing API tests; no client regressions in smoke testing
Rollback path validated: ability to switch reads back to JSONB-only view and delete added indexes within maintenance window
migration_plan: Design normalized schema in design doc and land initial CREATE TABLE migrations in a feature branch
Add columns/tables and lightweight triggers that mirror writes from application (dual-write) behind feature flag
Run small-scale backfill in staging and measure throughput; tune chunking/parallelism
Canary: run dual-write + backfill against 5 production-like tenants with traffic shaping
If canary stable, scale backfill across remaining tenants during off-peak hours; continuously monitor WAL and replication lag
Flip read routing: point read queries at compatibility view that prefers normalized columns but falls back to JSONB if null
After 2 weeks of stable metrics, remove JSONB usage in service code and drop legacy JSONB keys in a maintenance window
rollback_plan: If error spike or sustained latency regression: pause new backfill batches and disable dual-write triggers
Switch read routing back to JSONB-first view within <15 minutes
Revert schema migrations that added non-essential indexes in a controlled maintenance window
Run a short postmortem and fix data correctness issues before resuming backfill
If WAL or replication problems persist, open escalation with DBA/infra and restore last known-good configuration
performance_targets: Reduce average hot-table row width by >= 30%
Decrease 95th percentile read latency for tenant-prefetch path by >= 20%
Lower write amplification (WAL bytes) for frequent update paths by >= 15% after migration
Backfill throughput >= 50k rows/min for parallelized worker pool in prod-like infra
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: backfill progress, per-tenant lag, WAL bytes/sec, replication lag, 99th read latency for affected queries
Alerts: replication_lag > 30s for >5 minutes, backfill_task_failure rate > 1% over 10m, increased error rate on canary tenants > 0.5%
Runbook: step-by-step to pause backfill, disable triggers, revert read routing, and engage DBA on high WAL/lag
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Dual-write divergence. Mitigation: idempotent backfill with checksum comparison and reconciler job
Risk: Increased WAL and replication lag during backfill. Mitigation: throttle parallelism, run during off-peak, and use logical replication slots with max_lag guard
Risk: Query plan regressions after adding new joins. Mitigation: introduce selective partial indexes and run explain-based profiling before flip
Risk: Client-facing regressions. Mitigation: compatibility view and extensive end-to-end smoke tests
technical_decisions: Use separate normalized tables (entity_props) rather than adding wide nullable columns to keep row width predictable
Backfill implemented as idempotent, chunked worker DAG in Airflow with tenant-aware concurrency
Dual-write implemented at service layer behind a feature flag for early validation; supplemented by DB triggers for safety
Compatibility layer: SQL view that prefers normalized columns, then falls back to JSONB via COALESCE to avoid client changes
Indexes: start with partial indexes (tenant_id IS NOT NULL AND extracted_field IS NOT NULL) to limit maintenance cost
